crime: When {WITCH_NAME} was small, a doctor felt every bone in her and told her mother, "Nothing's broken. She's just made wrong." If no one could find it, it was all of her.

Only one girl wanted her touch: the mender. Every evening in the lounge she sat with her darning hoop over the girls' torn and cracked things, and wherever {WITCH_NAME}'s hand raised a dark line, the mender fixed it the moment it showed. Then she dozed over her work until the girls fetched it before lockup.

At nine one night, {WITCH_NAME} brought her own crooked dress. Her touch raised no line anywhere on it. The mender turned it over. "Nothing's torn. It isn't broken, it's just made wrong." She handed it back and took up the next girl's cup.
At ten past nine, alone with her in the lounge, {WITCH_NAME} drove the mender's temple against the fireplace stone, then sat her up in her chair, mending in her lap, as if dozing.

At twenty to ten she came back with the girls fetching their mending and laid her fingers on the sleeping mender's sleeved wrist. No line rose anywhere on her. "Let her sleep," she said, and stayed among them until lockup.
At ten to ten, a prisoner went back to wake the mender for lockup and found her dead, without a mark on her.

In the trial court, {WITCH_NAME} laid her hand on the dead girl's forehead, and a line rose across her temple, tracing a cracked skull. The prisoners ruled that it had cracked after twenty to ten: her bare touch raised every hidden break, none had risen then, and from then until lockup she had been among them.

Then a prisoner noticed a fine dark line on the dead girl's cuff, along a snapped thread, left unmended where {WITCH_NAME}'s fingers had rested at twenty to ten. Her touch had read the sleeve, not the girl. The skull was already cracked.
fields.epitaph: Every line her touch raised, the mender mended—except the one she raised on the mender herself.
execution: The execution stand raises a darning hoop taller than she is. She is wound into it with darning thread, her palms flat on her chest.
A darning needle comes through her chest between her fingers, then back, then through again, darning back and forth. Her palms, still flat on her chest, raise a dark line along every pass.
The needle draws the last stitch tight and stops. She hangs still in the hoop, darned shut beneath her hands and their dark lines.

magic.name: Fault Lines
magic.text: Her touch raises every hidden crack or injury in a person or thing to the surface as a dark line.
